registration: T-R5 10b5-1 plan terminations, half A, v1
sealed: Strategist draft 2026-11-04; operator approval by running Sprint R5-2 (RUN-IS-APPROVAL)
look_budget: one Stage R registered look, the second drawn forward from the Q1 2027 allowance; one Q1 look remains after it; Stage R stands at four nils of six before this look
question: after an officer's or director's termination of a Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement becomes PUBLIC (the 10-Q or 10-K that discloses it), does the stock earn a positive abnormal return over the next 60 trading days that a reader of the filing could have captured? The private drift between termination and disclosure is reported, not voted.
prior: the pre-2023 literature finds positive abnormal returns after terminations of selling plans (insiders stop selling before good news); most plans are selling plans; whether anything survives the public disclosure date is the open question

data.prices: Sharadar snapshot_20261004p bulk_stocks.parquet sha256 b5ed7140b6c08a1fcb2d03e81bde22db0ef2d0a551c61e0816ebc05f4c602ad4; closeadj for returns; closeunadj and volume for tradability; dates 1997-12-31 to 2026-10-02; frozen, no refresh inside this look
data.tickers: bulk_tickers.parquet sha256 61d14f069da12fa950bc83970f7d52b0f617b87c737e79a7657f37344a10e8a0; CIK from the secfilings URL; permaticker and ticker from the same row
data.calendar: trading days are the distinct dates in bulk_stocks; D+k and T-k are counted in trading days

event_definition.row_filter: a row of events.parquet with rule10b51_terminated_flag true or nonrule10b51_terminated_flag true, AND neither adoption flag true in the same row, AND a parseable tagged termination date T, AND file_date minus T >= 0 calendar days, AND form in {10-Q, 10-K}
event_definition.direction_filter: PURCHASE-PLAN rows are excluded: the row's text block, lower-cased, contains 'purchase' or 'buy' and contains none of 'sale', 'sell', 'sold'; rows with neither family or both are kept; the three-way split is reported
event_definition.disclosure_date: D = file_date; if D is not a trading day, the next trading day
event_definition.one_event_per_filing: events are unique on (permaticker, D); several individuals in one filing are one event; the individual count is kept as a column
event_definition.issuer_mapping: CIK to bulk_tickers rows with table == SEP via secfilings; if several permatickers, keep the one whose ticker has a bulk_stocks row on D+1 and, if still several, the most rows before D; if none, drop
event_definition.history: at least 250 bulk_stocks rows for the ticker dated before T
event_definition.tradability: closeunadj on D+1 >= 2.00 USD and the median of closeunadj times volume over the 20 trading days ending D >= 500000 USD
event_definition.completeness: closeadj present on every trading day from D+1 to D+61 inclusive; events failing this are dropped and counted
event_definition.halves: half A: 2023-07-01 <= D <= 2025-03-31 (this look); half B: 2025-04-01 <= D <= 2026-06-30, UNOPENED, one confirmation look only on SOMETHING; holdout: D >= 2026-07-01 and every later filing, SEALED and growing
event_definition.minimum_events: if half A holds fewer than 200 events after all filters, HALT at resolution; no look spent

returns.market: the equal-weight mean daily log return across all bulk_stocks tickers with closeunadj >= 1.00 USD on the prior day and at least 250 prior rows; built once from the snapshot and cached with its sha256 reported
returns.voted_window: entry at the close of D+1, exit at the close of D+61: the sum of the 60 abnormal daily log returns from D+2 to D+61
returns.cost: 20 bps round trip (10 a side) subtracted from every event's voted-window return
returns.reported_windows: the 20-day window D+2 to D+21; the pre-disclosure window from the close of T (or the next trading day) to the close of D+1; the pre-termination window from the close of T-21 to the close of T; the mean abnormal path at 5, 10, 20, 40 and 60 days after D+1

statistic.mCAR: the equal-weight mean across events of the net voted-window abnormal log return; the quantity the null votes on
statistic.descriptives: median, share positive, the reported windows, events by filing month, the direction split, title substring mix; reported, not adjudicated

voting_null.name: common-shift pseudo-events
voting_null.mechanism: each replicate shifts EVERY event's D by the same integer k trading days, k drawn uniformly from the union of [-378, -126] and [126, 378]; the same stocks, windows and cost at dates where no disclosure happened; a shifted window lying inside T-60 to D+61 of any real event of the same issuer is dropped from that replicate; a replicate retaining fewer than 90 percent of events is redrawn
voting_null.p: the share of replicates whose mCAR is >= the observed mCAR
voting_null.what_it_asks: whether these stocks earn more in the 60 days after their disclosure dates than in the same windows at other times, with the clustering of events in filing months preserved
voting_null.why_common_shift: independent per-event shifts would destroy the correlation between events that share filing months and make the null too narrow

order_of_operations: 1. RESOLUTION: the event set is resolved and counted at every clause; no return of any event is computed
2. MARKET INDEX: built and cached; not an event statistic
3. MDE: (null p95 - null median) + 0.8416 * sd(null mCAR), the null generated around the real D's without computing the observed mCAR
4. KNOWN-NULL CONTROL: 200 pseudo-event sets (each a common-shift draw) fed in as the observed set, each against a fresh 500-replicate null; the share at p <= 0.05 must lie in [0.01, 0.10] or HALT

5. POSITIVE CONTROL: on the real event set, add to each event's voted-window return a planted drift drawn per event from Uniform(0, 2X), X calibrated on ONE draw so the planted mean is about 0.03; then 50 fresh draws against fresh 500-replicate nulls; detection at p <= 0.05 must be >= 0.80 or HALT
6. OBSERVED: only then, and only on a pass receipt from steps 4 and 5

positive_control.leak: DELIBERATE and named by a test: the plant is added to the very window the vote reads

halts.fewer_than_200_events: HALT at resolution; no look spent
halts.known_null_outside_band: HALT before the observed read; no look spent; no ledger row
halts.positive_control_below_floor: HALT before the observed read; no look spent; no ledger row; the design returns to the Strategist

verdict.materiality: mCAR >= 0.015 net (1.5 percent over 60 trading days)
verdict.SOMETHING: p <= 0.05 AND mCAR >= 0.015 -> promoted to one registered half-B look
verdict.SIGNIFICANT_IMMATERIAL: p <= 0.05 AND 0 < mCAR < 0.015 -> recorded, not promoted; a nil for discovery
verdict.SUGGESTIVE: p in (0.05, 0.10] AND mCAR > 0 -> recorded, not promoted

interpretation_rulings.ruling: a row whose termination date lies after its filing date is a scheduled end, not a termination, excluded by the lag clause; a row carrying both an adoption and a termination flag is a modification, excluded by the no-adoption clause
when D or T is not a trading day the next trading day is used; windows are counted in trading days
all returns are log returns of closeadj and the bar is on the mean net abnormal log return, so no arithmetic overstatement enters
the vote is long over every kept row; purchase-plan rows are excluded by the text rule and nothing else is classified

ledger.row_schema: run_t_r3.py's, unchanged; ls_net_mean_bps carries mCAR in bps; p_premium carries the common-shift p
